summary: E2E tested user avatar upload feature (backend + frontend). All 6 backend pytest cases pass (upload, /auth/me carries avatar, login carries avatar, clear, 401 no-auth, 413 too-large). All frontend flows pass: default letter 'A', upload flow (JPEG data-URL), header + dropdown large avatar both update, persistence across reload and re-login, remove flow with confirm dialog + toast, validation rejects non-image and >8MB files, no regression on Dashboard/KMZ/MikroTik/Broadband pages (header user-avatar present on all).

issues: Recharts console warning spam: 'The width(-1) and height(-1) of chart should be greater than 0' — pre-existing, not related to this iteration but worth fixing (minWidth/minHeight on ResponsiveContainer parent)

action_items: Optional: Validation message for non-image file whose extension is .png but content is text currently shows 'Gagal membaca gambar' (image decode failed) rather than 'File harus berupa gambar…'. Browser infers image/png mime from extension so the mime pre-check doesn't fire. Consider also validating via magic bytes or clarifying copy. Non-blocking — upload is still rejected and no request is fired.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py line 417: `len(avatar) > 2_500_000` uses character length of data-URL, which is ~1.87MB decoded; comment/error message says ~1.5MB — consider aligning the numbers.
Header.jsx imports and downscale logic are fine; consider revoking Object URLs after canvas draw (minor mem hygiene).
Existing Recharts ResponsiveContainer warnings across pages are unrelated but noisy in the console — worth adding minHeight.
seed_data_creation: None. Test resets/clears avatar via API before frontend run and leaves the user with cleared avatar at end.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend tests for avatar live in /app/backend/tests/test_avatar.py — reuse for regression. Frontend selectors: data-testid=user-avatar (header circle), header-user-menu (dropdown trigger), avatar-upload-button, avatar-file-input, avatar-remove-button, avatar-remove-confirm. Client resizes to JPEG 320x320 so uploaded src starts with 'data:image/jpeg'. Login/auth/me both return avatar_base64.
